source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek (VVZ) – Czech Public Procurement Bulletin
why_relevant: Legally mandated publication venue under zák. 134/2016 Sb. for contract notices (oznámení o zahájení zadávacího řízení) and award notices (oznámení o výsledku zadávacího řízení) above/below EU thresholds. Any public-sector banking, acquiring, payment-terminal or payment-infrastructure contract must surface here first, with CPV codes, estimated value, awarded supplier and price.

source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek – NIPEZ instance (vvz.nipez.cz)
why_relevant: The VVZ operated by MMR under the NIPEZ umbrella; appears to be the current/parallel technical entry point for the uveřejňovací subsystém (publication subsystem) and eForms-era notice forms. Same legal notice corpus as vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz but a distinct host worth tracking so a platform migration does not silently break collection.

source_name: NEN – Národní elektronický nástroj (National Electronic Tool)
why_relevant: State-operated e-procurement platform where a large share of central-government and many municipal authorities run the whole procedure. Contract detail pages carry zadávací dokumentace (tender documents), technical specifications, Q&A, bid-opening records and award data — far richer than a VVZ notice. Confirmed to contain payment-acceptance tenders, e.g. card-acceptance and terminal-rental services and cashier/POS system deliveries.

source_name: Věstník NEN
why_relevant: NEN's own bulletin view of notices published from the platform — a chronological, filterable stream that is the lowest-latency way to catch newly launched banking/payment procedures inside NEN before they propagate elsewhere.

source_name: Registr DNS (NEN dynamic purchasing systems register)
why_relevant: Central register of dynamické nákupní systémy (DNS) run in NEN. DNS/framework agreements are how much Czech public ICT and payment-hardware buying actually happens: a vendor admitted to a DNS then wins repeated mini-tenders that may never appear as standalone headline notices. Tracking DNS scope + admitted suppliers reveals the medium-term competitive field for payment infrastructure.

source_name: ISVZ – Informační systém o veřejných zakázkách (statistics + open data)
why_relevant: Statutory information system (§224 zák. 134/2016 Sb.) offering market overviews, central registers, a contracting-authority-profile validator, and an OpenData section. This is the bulk/structured route into the same notice corpus — far better for systematic time-series collection than scraping notice HTML.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (portal-vz.cz) – MMR methodology hub
why_relevant: Ministry for Regional Development's authoritative map of the NIPEZ ecosystem: which subsystem publishes what, the uveřejňovací subsystém, IS VZ, NIPEZ commodity catalogue, methodologies, decision databases and annual reports on the state of public procurement. Best single starting node for snowballing further CZ procurement sources and for understanding what is legally required to be published where.

source_name: NIPEZ podpora – Registr veřejných zakázek (rules & data structures)
why_relevant: Documents the Registr veřejných zakázek: the central record that ingests contract data from all certified electronic tools (not just NEN) and redistributes it to consumers, per MMR-issued data-structure descriptions. Essential for designing collection: it defines the schema and the machine-readable path to the full national corpus including private e-tools.

source_name: Národní katalog otevřených dat (NKOD) – data.gov.cz
why_relevant: National open-data catalogue that indexes procurement-adjacent datasets (confirmed to carry e.g. the ÚOHS decision collection dataset). Use it to discover which procurement/contract datasets are officially published, by whom, in what format, and with what licence — a licence-and-provenance layer over the raw portals.

source_name: Registr smluv (smlouvy.gov.cz) via portal.gov.cz service
why_relevant: Statutory contract register: public bodies must publish contracts above CZK 50,000 excl. VAT, and an unpublished contract is legally ineffective. This is where the actual signed acquiring/terminal/banking-service contract text, pricing schedules and annexes appear — often the only place the real commercial terms of an awarded tender become visible.

source_name: Hlídač státu – Hlídač veřejných zakázek & Hlídač smluv (API)
why_relevant: NGO aggregator that normalises the contract register, the public-procurement register and ÚOHS decisions into one searchable corpus with a documented public API — dramatically cheaper to query than the official portals, and it links suppliers to contracts to political/ownership context. Best used as an accelerator and cross-check, with official registers as the source of truth.

source_name: ÚOHS – Sbírky rozhodnutí (public procurement review decisions)
why_relevant: The competition/procurement review authority's decision collection (since 1999). Challenged tenders produce decisions that expose evaluation criteria disputes, technical-specification bias claims and bid pricing — an unusually rich indirect window into how banking/payment tenders were actually structured and contested, and which suppliers fight.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (CZ notices, CPV-filtered)
why_relevant: Above-EU-threshold Czech notices are forwarded to TED, giving a machine-readable, multilingual, eForms-structured duplicate of the highest-value CZ banking/payment tenders — with a stable API and CPV taxonomy. Excellent cross-border comparability layer and a hedge against CZ-portal scraping fragility.

source_name: E-ZAK (QCM) certified electronic tool – multi-authority profiles
why_relevant: One of the dominant certified elektronické nástroje in CZ; hundreds of ministries, regions, hospitals and utilities run their profil zadavatele on an E-ZAK instance (each on its own subdomain). Many banking/payment tenders live only as a VVZ pointer plus the full documentation on an E-ZAK profile. Confirmed instances include the Czech National Bank (ezak.cnb.cz) and the Ministry of Agriculture (zakazky.eagri.cz).

source_name: TENDER ARENA (Tender systems s.r.o.)
why_relevant: Second major commercial certified e-tool / profil zadavatele host. Directly relevant to this cell: Národní rozvojová banka (the state development bank) publishes its procurement profile here, making it a must-track host for state-financial-institution buying.

source_name: Vhodné uveřejnění (vhodne-uverejneni.cz) – profil zadavatele host
why_relevant: Another widely used profil zadavatele host; carries a profile page for Česká národní banka (ICO 48136450). Profiles here are indexed by ICO, which makes it a convenient ICO-keyed entry point for tracking a named financial-sector contracting authority across time.

source_name: Gemin.cz – profil zadavatele / e-procurement tool
why_relevant: Certified e-tool used notably for small-scale contracts (veřejné zakázky malého rozsahu) — the tier where individual terminal purchases, payment-gateway subscriptions and small integration jobs sit, below VVZ publication duty. Reported as the profile address for the Czech National Bank. Small-scale contracts are precisely the layer that never reaches VVZ or TED.

source_name: E-ZAKAZKY.CZ
why_relevant: A further certified profil zadavatele provider in the fragmented CZ e-tool market. Included for completeness of the host inventory: because Czech authorities freely choose their e-tool, no single platform gives full coverage and the host list itself must be maintained as a source.

source_name: Česká národní banka – Veřejné zakázky / úřední deska
why_relevant: The central bank as a contracting authority under zák. 134/2016 Sb. Its tenders cover payment-system, cash-handling and financial IT infrastructure — the highest-signal single buyer in this cell. The page is the authoritative pointer to whichever e-tool profile currently hosts its contracts (E-ZAK instance ezak.cnb.cz observed).

source_name: Národní rozvojová banka (NRB) – Veřejné zakázky
why_relevant: State development bank (ICO 44848943) procuring banking IT, payment and back-office services as a public contracting authority; publishes via TENDER ARENA. A second high-signal financial-sector buyer distinct from commercial banks (which are not covered by procurement law).

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – Profil zadavatele / společný nákup
why_relevant: The Finance Ministry both procures state banking/treasury services and runs centralised/joint purchasing (společný nákup) for its resort — a structural driver of large aggregated payment and financial-service contracts. Central-purchasing pages reveal aggregation intent before individual notices appear.

source_name: Výroční zpráva o stavu veřejných zakázek v ČR (MMR annual report)
why_relevant: MMR's annual state-of-procurement report gives market-size, procedure-type and CPV-segment aggregates for the whole CZ procurement market — the baseline denominator against which banking/payment tender volumes should be read. Also circulated via EU channels in English, which helps cross-language validation.

source_name: NajdiVZ – CPV code browser (CZ)
why_relevant: Czech-language browser of the CPV taxonomy including the financial-and-insurance-services division. Practical utility: it gives the exact Czech labels for the CPV codes to filter on (bankovnictví 66110000, zpracování finančních transakcí a služby zúčtovacího střediska 66172000), which is what makes precise CZ-language querying of VVZ/NEN possible.

source_name: gov.cz service catalogue entry – Věstník veřejných zakázek
why_relevant: The official citizen-portal service card for VVZ. Useful as a stable, government-maintained pointer that names the current canonical VVZ endpoint and operator — a cheap way to detect when the bulletin migrates hosts (a real risk given the vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz / vvz.nipez.cz duality).

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (official EU procurement portal, search UI)
why_relevant: Single mandatory publication venue for all Czech above-threshold contract notices, award notices and modifications. Contains CZ banking/payment-services tenders (CPV 66xxxxx, 72xxxxxx for card/ATM systems) in structured, multilingual form, with buyer name, NUTS CZ region, value, procedure type and — in award notices — the winning supplier. This is the core A2 spine for the CZ cell.

source_name: TED Search API (docs.ted.europa.eu — API v3/latest)
why_relevant: The machine-readable route into TED. Documents the search endpoint, expert query language, field selection and paging — this is what turns the CZ banking/payments notice flow into a repeatable monitored feed rather than manual browsing. Also documents API-key management, which determines rate limits and whether unauthenticated polling is viable.
